newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. food agency appeals for North Korea aid.
newsitem.headline: U.N. food agency appeals for North Korea aid.

text.p: The U.N.'s food aid agency said on Wednesday it had launched an urgent appeal to raise $41.6 million for urgent supplies to stave off famine in North Korea.

The Rome-based World Food Progamme said in a statement that it hoped to raise 100,000 metric tonnes of aid for North Korea, where it said people were receiving a quarter of their minimum daily food needs.

"The situation is critical because if, as feared, food stocks run out in April or May then there is a very real possibility of famine," WFP deputy executive director Namanga Ngongi was quoted as saying in the statement.
"We hope the international community will respond quickly to the WFP appeal," said Ngongi.
The statement said that while the WFP supplies would only represent a fraction of North Korea's total food requirements, the aid would benefit 630,000 children for one year.

The rest of the aid would go to 250,000 farmers and 850,000 employees who would receive food for 160 work days as part of a "food for work" programme aimed at rehabilitating farm land damaged by devastating floods in 1995 and 1996.
The floods left half a million people homeless and destroyed some two million tonnes of grain, the statement said.
